bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: TruBridge regulatory approvals pending; large health systems slow to adopt full platform; payer API access limitations for collaboration; AI hallucination risks in clinical workflows; currency volatility (FX gain/loss impact); integration risk of TruBridge EHR into IKS platform
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; emphasized AI-native transformation as core moat; proud of operational leverage (revenue up 18.5%, headcount up 5.3%); optimistic on TruBridge synergy and rural market; transparent about AQuity GTM missteps and pivot; tone is founder-led, tech-obsessed, and outcome-driven
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1) 45% female workforce including 5 C-suite leaders is a strategic differentiator in a male-dominated tech-health space; 2) Scribble Select’s multi-variant design (autonomous + human-in-loop) is a rare industry-first that solves adoption plateau (50-60% usage → likely >80%); 3) TruBridge’s 15M+ patient data is the real moat, not AI — enables longitudinal labeled datasets for superior SLMs; 4) Rural outpatient care models (70% of TruBridge volume) directly transferable to IKS’s core physician group market
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated strategic intent of "Sustained EBITDA expansion without significant dilution of Equity".
- FCF Yield of 89.9% in Q1 FY27 vs 84.5% in Q1 FY26 and 62.1% in Q4 FY26.
- OCF and FCF are stated to be "adjusted for upfront guarantee payment of economic value add made to a customer, for Rs 1,430 mn in Q1 FY 27"; growth shown as 20.5% OCF YoY and 26.9% FCF YoY, though the underlying OCF/FCF chart values are not recoverable from the extract.
- Net Debt is a tracked outlook line; the Medium-Term Financial Outlook slide lists 5,534, 2,654 and 3,000 (INR Mn) alongside the three periods, but the label-to-column binding is lost in extraction.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Top 10 customers: INR452cr (53% of Q4 revenue), grew 28% YoY; Top 5: grew 18% YoY; 90% revenue from repeat clients; 450+ large enterprise clients; AQuity cross-sell: 1 full-platform win (Holyoke), 1 expansion (Mission Community), 1 land-and-expand win (top 5 health system in RCM/value-based care); AI features: Scribble Select (multi-variant scribing), MyCare Hub (multi-agent patient engagement), autonomous coding in 2 specialties, integrated with Epic
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Claims to be "The only Comprehensive platform that delegates all chores across the patient journey", spanning Pre-visit, Peri-visit, In between visits and Post-visit stages of the patient journey.
- Addresses a stated TAM of US$260bn with an Outsourced Market of US$34bn (CY2023), growing at 8% / 12% CAGR respectively (2023-2028E), against US Healthcare Expenditure of US$5tn (CY2024); TAM is defined as "Total Addressable Market for RCM, VBC, Patient, Coding and Client Services" per a Zinnov Report.
- Established client relationships: "85%+ Revenues from Repeat Customers" and "5+ Years" average vintage for Top 10 / Top 5 clients (as of Mar 31, 2026); repeat clients are defined as those who availed the platform in the previous period.
- Serves "600+/650+ Healthcare Organizations" (Q1 27/Q1 26) and "450+ Enterprise level customers"; note the deck's organisation count is lower in Q1 27 than Q1 26 without explanation.
- Strategy is framed as "5 strategic pillars of execution", covering a proprietary-model System of Action for the large medical group market, integrated SOA & System of Record (SOR) for the rural/community health system market, re-stratified growth levers, margin recovery via operating model transformation and synergies, and culture and leadership.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] TruBridge RCM & Coding Businesses appear as an owned unit requiring "Operating model Transformation", and its rural/community installed base is a named cross-sell target; the deck repeatedly cites "one-time acquisition costs" affecting Q1 FY27 margins but does not state the acquisition's price or terms.
- [Associate/Investment] The deck refers to "increased equity base from revaluation of Abridge" as a reason ROE declined, and reports a "Share of Profit/(Loss) from Associates (net of tax)" line, indicating an associate/minority holding that is not otherwise described.
- [Awards] AMGA Distinguished Corporate Partner Award 2026; Best CFO & Finance Strategy Excellence Awards 2026 for Excellence in Investor Relations (organisational) and Best CFO in Healthcare for Nithya Balasubramanian, Whole-time Director & Group CFO; 2026 Dallas-Fort Worth Titan 100 for Sachin K. Gupta, Founder & Global CEO.
- [Track record] "A decade of consistent profitable growth" with a stated 28.7% Revenue CAGR and 46.4% PAT CAGR; the deck does not state the exact period these CAGRs span.
- [Geography] Business is US-facing (US healthcare expenditure TAM, US clients, USD revenue reporting) while the registered office and workforce base are in India; revenue grew 20.7% YoY in INR against 12.0% in USD, indicating material currency translation effect.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 35% Q4 (from 34% FY25) despite INR38cr one-off TruBridge due diligence costs; cost leverage from 5.3% headcount growth vs 18.5% revenue growth; offshore model fully integrated from AQuity; FX hedge loss (INR12cr) partially offset by forex gain (INR35cr), net benefit INR23cr
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: implied >15% YoY for FY27 based on momentum; margin: EBITDA margin to stabilize near 34-35%; order inflow: expected to accelerate with TruBridge close and AQuity cross-sell; capex/commissioning: minimal capex; TruBridge integration to drive $162B rural market entry
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: TruBridge acquisition (rural healthcare EHR+AI platform); Certilytics partnership (payer-provider collaboration to reduce denials); MyCare Hub expansion into predictive resource optimization (ICU, OR, nurse utilization); SLMs built for rural care applicable to physician groups

deepdive.thesis: IKS delivered 18.5% YoY revenue growth and 39% PAT growth by scaling its AI-native platform while reducing headcount, with strategic wins in mid-sized health systems and a land-and-expand model for large systems; the pending TruBridge acquisition positions it to dominate rural healthcare with integrated EHR+AI, creating a unique data moat and cross-market synergy.

open.item: Company continues pruning the acquired AQuity client base toward a target ~500 core clients (down from 800+, now 640), with a couple hundred more to prune over at least a couple more quarters.
Full-year effective tax rate is likely to remain around 21% (Q2 ETR was 21%).

Global headcount was 12,368 FTEs, down ~7% YoY from 13,277 in Q1FY25 while growing revenue 16%; management expects the number to inch up over the rest of the year to support growth even as legacy optimization continues 2-3 more quarters.
Effective tax rate was 22% in Q1FY26 after losing tax breaks in one SEZ unit; management expects the ETR to remain in the same range for the full year.

Migration of AQuity customers to IKS ambient AI documentation and autonomous medical coding (across two specialties) should be largely completed over the rest of the fiscal, bringing EBITDA to steady state.
open.promised: largely complete by FY26 end text

open.item: The work of transforming AQuity's human-led delivery model to IKS tech-led (to lift EBITDA back to early/mid-30s) is roughly two-thirds done and moving faster than anticipated.
Revenue headwinds from AQuity tail-cutting and margin optimization should be completed by end of this fiscal (fiscal Q4FY26), after which growth returns to pure organic growth.
Intentionally pruning the AQuity long-tail customer base down from ~650 toward a steady-state of ~500 customers; expects roughly another two-to-three quarters to complete.
Management expects EBITDA margins to reach and stabilize in the early-to-mid-30s%; Q1 came in at 32% and management does not expect margins to improve beyond early-to-mid-30s.
Right-size total customer base to the 550-600 range (from 700 at Mar-2025, originally 850) by cutting AQuity's sub-scale clients.
Effective tax rate expected around 21%-22% in FY26 (vs 19% in FY25) due to loss of tax breaks on one SEZ unit.
Transform AQuity's operating model to lift blended EBITDA margins to the early 30s over a period of time (Q4FY25 already at ~31%).
Continue cutting small AQuity clients and transforming remaining customers from US-headcount to tech-led offshore model through the larger part of FY26.
All things remaining equal (absent tuck-in acquisitions or new customer capital deployments), IKS expects to become debt free sometime in the next fiscal year (FY26).

Management expects consolidated EBITDA margins to stabilize in the early-to-mid 30s, and having reached ~31% ahead of the original 18-24 month glide path, now expects to reach that steady state within about a year.
Additional TruBridge due-diligence and legal transaction expenses expected to hit again in Q1 (FY27) as regulatory approvals are still work in progress.
